title: Guards Sweeping a Line of Posts
src: Media.net OA, IIT Guwahati (from a candidate's note), question 3. The note asked for each thief's waiting time; the mock asks for the minimum total, which is well defined (the same problem as Codeforces 311B).
body:
Posts 1, 2, …, N stand on a line; the distance from post k to post k+1 is dist[k-1]. There are P guards and M thieves. Thief i arrives at post node[i] at time arrive[i] and then waits there.

Each guard starts from post 1 at a moment of your choosing (any integer, even negative) and walks towards post N at speed 1 without ever stopping. A guard passing a post catches every thief already waiting there. A thief caught at time T has waited T − arrive[i].

Choose the guards' start times so that every thief is caught, minimising the total waiting time. Return that minimum.

Function to complete

Complete minTotalWait(P, dist, node, arrive). It returns the minimum total waiting time.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
inp: Line 1: P. Line 2: K = N − 1. Line 3: dist[0..K-1]. Line 4: M. Then M lines: node[i] arrive[i].
out: One integer: the minimum total waiting time.

wrong.why: uses only one guard whatever P is

samples.ex: Post 2 is 2 away from post 1, post 3 is 5 away. With one guard leaving at time 2: post 1 at 2 (that thief waited 2), post 2 at 4 (waited 0), post 3 at 7 (waited 2). Total 4, and no start time does better.
Two guards: one leaves at time 0 for the thieves at posts 1 and 3, one at time 2 for the thief at post 2. Nobody waits.
